name: Drew Uher
profile: Drew Uher founded HomeLight in San Francisco in 2012 after he and his wife struggled to find a well-matched agent when buying a home. HomeLight matches consumers with real estate agents using transaction data and has added direct home buying and financing; it was valued at $1.6B in 2021 and is now headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona.
interesting_fact: Uher says his one non-negotiable habit is not working on planes: 'It's the only time I really have to myself.' He now leads HomeLight's AI efforts including an AI-powered 'Buy Before You Sell' bridge loan.
deep_cut_fact: Before HomeLight he co-founded Gameyola, a distribution and monetization platform for casual Flash games that reached 250,000 daily active users; earlier he covered real estate and mortgage stocks in Morgan Stanley's New York research division. He is also a licensed California real estate broker.
notes: Texas A&M (MIS) and Stanford MBA. Best route is HomeLight press team.

name: Mark Shaw
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Inclined (per The Org profile; Strava co-founder)
profile: Mark Shaw was part of Strava's 2009 founding team alongside Mark Gainey, Michael Horvath, Davis Kitchel, Chris Donahue and Pelle Sommansson. Per his professional profile he was Strava's CTO 2009-2017 and head of growth 2017-2019, after earlier co-founding Guidewire Software; since 2020 he has been co-founder and CTO of Inclined.
interesting_fact: Michael Horvath's 2023 open letter announcing his CEO succession named Shaw among the six-person founding team that started Strava in 2009.
deep_cut_fact: Before Strava he started as a software engineer at Kana Software (1997-2001) and co-founded insurance-software firm Guidewire in 2001; he holds BS (1996) and MS (1998) degrees in computer science from Stanford.
notes: Low public profile; career details come from The Org aggregator profile (not self-published), treat dates as approximate. Strava press form is only an indirect route since he appears to have left Strava ~2019. Alive status not explicitly confirmed (no reports of death).

name: Harry Jones
current_role: Co-founder, Motorway (former Chief Product Officer; current operating role not confirmed)
profile: Harry Jones co-founded Motorway, the London-based online used-car marketplace connecting private sellers with dealers, with Tom Leathes (CEO) and Alex Buttle; it reached a ~$1B valuation. Motorway was the trio's fifth startup together. TechCrunch notes Jones is no longer Motorway's CPO; no new venture was confirmed.
interesting_fact: Motorway began as a simple instant car-valuation price-comparison site; the team then cold-called dealers to find buyers before pivoting to its dealer marketplace model. Jones: 'That pivot was really critical in how we kind of evolved the company.'
deep_cut_fact: Jones, Leathes and Buttle met in 2002 and have built five startups together (two acquired), with earlier ideas including a travel-accommodation curation service and an office-space search site; their method is to ship cheap one-page websites fast and double down on whatever gets traction.
notes: Common name; ensure outreach targets the Motorway co-founder. Tom Leathes is Motorway's public face; Jones has stepped back from CPO role.

name: Zheng Jie
current_role: Founder, chairman & president, Shulan Medical Group (树兰医疗), Hangzhou
profile: Zheng Jie (郑杰) co-founded Shulan Medical in Hangzhou in 2013, building a private hospital group around Shulan (Hangzhou), Anji and Quzhou hospitals; backers include Sequoia China and Qiming, at an ~8B yuan valuation, and the group has filed for a Hong Kong IPO. A serial entrepreneur in health IT, he is pushing Shulan's 2025 'All in Technology' strategy around computational medicine.
interesting_fact: Zheng frames his vision as moving medicine from 'seeing a doctor' to 'counting diseases', via a 'self-developed system - data driven - AI enabled' model built on computational medicine and high-performance computing.
deep_cut_fact: He took part in China's national 863 Program researching digital-healthcare and medical-information standards, launched the OMAHA (Open Medical and Health Alliance) in 2015, founded what is described as China's first non-profit digital-healthcare research institute, and introduced a 'Computational Medicine' course at Shulan.
notes: Common Chinese name; identity confirmed via Shulan founder references. The name Shulan combines characters from the names of academicians Zheng Shusen and Li Lanjuan (source: news.pedaily.cn/202308/520963.shtml). No published contact found; Chinese-language outreach via Shulan Medical corporate channels / HK IPO sponsors likely needed. Data-driven medicine angle fits a data-center podcast.

name: Michael Suffredini
current_role: Co-founder, board member and advisor, Axiom Space (CEO until Aug 2024)
profile: Mike Suffredini spent decades at NASA, including as International Space Station program manager (2005-2015), overseeing completion of ISS assembly. In 2016 he co-founded Houston-based Axiom Space with Kam Ghaffarian to build the first commercial space station, and led it as president/CEO; he stepped down as CEO in August 2024 and remains a board member and advisor.
interesting_fact: His honors include the NASA Distinguished Service Medal, Presidential Meritorious and Distinguished Executive ranks, the National Air and Space Museum Trophy and the Yuri Gagarin Medal.
deep_cut_fact: After watching Neil Armstrong land on the Moon as a child he wanted to be a 'space guy'; at UT Austin (aerospace engineering, 1983) he originally aimed at high-performance aircraft until studying orbital dynamics under Victor Szebehely pulled him toward space. He also created NASA's ISS Research Office.
notes: Stepped back from CEO 'for personal reasons' (Axiom release Aug 2024) - avoid probing. Axiom now markets orbital data centers, a strong hook for an energy/data-center podcast. Current Axiom CEO is Tejpaul Bhatia (since Apr 2025).

name: Sebastian Rymarz
current_role: President, Essor (formed 2024 when Branded acquired Heyday); co-founder & CEO of Heyday
profile: Sebastian Rymarz co-founded San Francisco-based Heyday with Adam Gerchen in August 2020 to acquire and scale marketplace-native (mainly Amazon) consumer brands; it raised about $800M including a $555M Series C in 2021, reportedly at a $1B+ valuation. In September 2024 Branded acquired Heyday to form Essor, a ~$400M-revenue consumer products group where Rymarz became president.
interesting_fact: Heyday emerged from stealth with a $175M Series A just three months after founding; Rymarz called it 'the early days of a tectonic shift toward marketplace commerce.' Unlike rivals, he said Heyday would buy only one or two brands a month to focus on growing each.
deep_cut_fact: In 2022 Heyday bought ZitSticka, the direct-to-consumer acne-patch brand, as part of its push into personal care.
notes: Merger quote: 'Joining forces with Branded strengthens our platform, and, importantly, our balance sheet' (happi.com). Aggregator profiles mention prior roles at Fundbox and TPG Sixth Street, unverified. No published press email found; Essor corporate channels are best route.

name: Lauris Liberts
current_role: Founder and co-owner, Draugiem Group; co-founder and board chair of Printful
profile: Latvian tech entrepreneur Lauris Liberts founded the social network draugiem.lv and created Draugiem Group in 2004. In 2013 the group incubated Printful, a print-on-demand and drop-shipping fulfilment service he co-founded with Davis Siksnans; it became Latvia's first unicorn after a $130M investment from Bregal Sagemount in 2021.
interesting_fact: Printful grew out of the team's own side businesses Startup Vitamins and Behappy.me, which sold motivational quote posters and prints; needing a reliable print-and-ship partner, they built their own and launched Printful on July 16, 2013.
deep_cut_fact: He studied economics at the University of Latvia and earned a master's in e-business and innovation from Lancaster University in the UK.
notes: Chair/board role at Printful per MarketScreener aggregator. Draugiem Group (draugiemgroup.com) and Printful press page (printful.com/press) are JS-rendered; no published email extracted. Route via Draugiem Group or Printful press team.

name: Yao Wenchun
current_role: Co-founder, executive director & Chief Risk Officer, XTransfer (listed in the 2026 HKEX prospectus coverage as 姚伟春 / Yao Weichun)
profile: XTransfer, a Shanghai-founded B2B cross-border trade payments platform for small exporters, was started in 2017 by Bill Deng (邓国标) and fellow ex-Ant Group/Alibaba staff. Its co-founder and CRO 姚伟春 previously ran risk at Ant Group. XTransfer reached a $3.02B valuation after a Series E in March 2026 and filed for a Hong Kong main-board IPO in April 2026.
interesting_fact: XTransfer's 2017 seed round was just $2.95M at a $12M post-money valuation (from Yunqi Partners and Gaorong); its 2026 Series E valued it at $3.02B.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding XTransfer, Yao was at Ant Group heading international risk and merchant risk management and leading its business-intelligence department.
notes: Name mismatch: input says 'Yao Wenchun' but XTransfer's prospectus coverage names the co-founder/CRO 姚伟春 (Yao Weichun); ZoomInfo also lists 'Weichun Yao'. Very likely the same person (XTransfer valuation matches) but verify. XTransfer site publishes only helpdesk@xtransfer.com (customer support), no press email.

name: Ghislain de Fontenay
current_role: Co-founder and Director of the Innovation Lab ('Delta Team'), PayFit (former CTO)
profile: Ghislain de Fontenay co-founded Paris-based PayFit in 2015 with Firmin Zocchetto and Florian Fournier to automate payroll and HR for European SMEs, serving as its first CTO. PayFit became a unicorn after raising EUR 254M in late 2021. He now leads PayFit's innovation lab.
interesting_fact: To tame French payroll rules, PayFit's founders created their own programming language, JetLang, to encode labour regulations and collective agreements, later extended to other countries.
deep_cut_fact: He and Firmin Zocchetto built their first company together as high-school students: a social network for learning foreign languages, which they dropped because it became too time-consuming.
notes: Current Innovation Lab title comes from an aggregator profile (me.sh); low public profile, technical founder. PayFit press contact published as mailto on its press page.

name: Javier Suarez
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Oliva (workplace mental health platform); co-founder and former CPO of TravelPerk (now Perk)
profile: Javier Suarez co-founded Barcelona-based business travel platform TravelPerk in 2015 with Avi Meir and Ron Levin, serving as chief product officer; it later reached a multi-billion-dollar valuation. In 2020 he co-founded Oliva with Sancar Sahin, an employee wellbeing platform offering therapy and workshops used in 27+ countries and 14 languages, backed by Molten Ventures and Stride VC.
interesting_fact: TravelPerk was born from an observation at Booking.com: the founders, both ex-Booking employees, saw that the company focused on leisure travel while business travel was a poorly served market.
deep_cut_fact: Before TravelPerk he worked at Booking.com in business development; his co-founder Avi Meir had joined Booking when it acquired Meir's startup Hotel Ninjas in 2014.
notes: Now focused on Oliva (CEO). He has spoken publicly about founder burnout as Oliva's origin; let him lead on that topic. Sources differ on his Booking.com role (product performance & innovation vs business development). No published press email found.

name: Frederico Amaral
current_role: Founder & CEO, Lerian (São Paulo); co-founder and former Chief Product & Technology Officer of Dock
profile: Fred Amaral co-founded Brazilian payments and banking-as-a-service infrastructure firm Dock, which became a unicorn, and served as its Chief Product & Technology Officer. He left to found Lerian with his own capital in 2023; it builds Midaz, a source-available core-banking ledger, and raised an R$18M seed led by Maya Capital in 2024 plus a further round reported in 2026.
interesting_fact: With Lerian he is betting that core banking goes open: Midaz's code is public and Lerian plans to earn mainly from hosting and add-on features, building a developer community through developer advocacy and workshops.
deep_cut_fact: He personally pitched Midaz to Brazil's developer community on TabNews, the Brazilian dev forum, in posts like 'Midaz: open source banking ledger com múltiplos conectores'.
notes: Goes by 'Fred Amaral'. Lerian email is the company's general contact, not personal. Aggregator profiles mention earlier stints at Uber, Deutsche Bank, BTG Pactual and Movile (unverified).

name: Jonathan Siddharth
profile: Jonathan Siddharth co-founded Turing in 2018 (incubated at Foundation Capital) to source, vet and manage remote software developers with AI. Turing has since pivoted to supplying coding and reasoning data and talent to frontier AI labs such as OpenAI, raising a $111M Series E led by Khazanah Nasional in March 2025 at a $2.2B valuation, with a ~$300M revenue run rate.
interesting_fact: In 2012, needing mobile engineers for his first startup, he hired developers from Ukraine, Serbia and China; their app was recognized by Apple as one of the best in the App Store, an experience that seeded Turing's 'Talent Cloud' idea.
deep_cut_fact: His career began with an internship on Yahoo's search relevance team, then ranking work at natural-language search startup Powerset (acquired by Microsoft); in 2008 he co-founded content-discovery app Rover, acquired by Revcontent in 2016. He has also served on Quora's board and advised through Stanford's StartX.
notes: Strong fit for AI/data-center angle: Turing is a key training-data/coding provider for LLM labs. Stanford MS in CS (ML and search). Active writer (Unite.AI author page).

name: João Pedro Resende
profile: Belo Horizonte-born computer scientist João Pedro Resende co-founded Hotmart in 2011 with university classmate Mateus Bicalho, building a platform that bundles payments, hosting and delivery for creators selling courses, ebooks and other digital products. Hotmart Company, which also owns Teachable and eNotas, sells into ~190 countries; global HQ moved to the Netherlands in 2016. He still leads it, now pushing AI tools.
interesting_fact: Resende and Bicalho were early figures in 'San Pedro Valley', the Belo Horizonte tech hub that grew from startups clustering in the São Pedro neighborhood.
deep_cut_fact: His first startup, MobWorks (2004, with Bicalho), tried to build mobile apps and failed; at the same time he ran an online gaming forum, where he learned traffic, site optimization and monetization, lessons that fed into Hotmart.
notes: Known as 'JP Resende'. Hosts the annual Hotmart FIRE creator conference in Belo Horizonte (11th edition in 2026). Portuguese-language outreach recommended.

name: Salman Rehmetullah
profile: Sal Rehmetullah co-founded Orlando-based payments company Stax with his sister Suneera Madhani in 2014; after nearly 10 years it had over $140M recurring revenue, $245M raised and a $1.1B+ valuation, and the siblings exited in 2023. They now run Worth, an AI platform that automates SMB underwriting, onboarding and verification for banks and fintechs; it raised a $20M seed led by TTV Capital in 2025.
interesting_fact: On Worth's edge: 'We have the full 360 financial data of a small business, which has been nonexistent.' Worth pre-fills applications and automates KYB, ownership identity, fraud, bank-account and real-time financial statement checks.
deep_cut_fact: Stax and its sibling co-founders were EY Entrepreneur Of The Year 2021 Florida finalists.
notes: Goes by 'Sal'. Has a Qwoted expert-source page (app.qwoted.com/sources/sal-rehmetullah), a possible journalist-facing route. Avoid the 2023 Stax exit circumstances. EY finalist fact is from the press-release title (page body was blocked).
